decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY capturing the separate requirement for sufficient routing space. Retaining a through-hole breakout for every ESP32-S3 pin does not establish an additional form-factor value or confirm a new pin pitch.
Reusing the main board as a general ESP32-S3 base platform does not alter the current three-board architecture, assigned board roles, or main-board exclusions.
Full through-hole pin access and platform reuse do not change the established requirement to place the ESP32 antenna at the PCB edge.
The source decision concerns the ESP32 breakout on the main board and has no effect on the power board's dimensions, mounting, orientation, or connector placement.
Retaining access to every ESP32-S3 pin does not change the established placement and alignment rules for the main-board and sensor-board connectors.
The main-board ESP32 breakout decision does not alter the power board's four-layer stack requirement.
The source does not change the standalone USB regulator, activation condition, powered rail, powered loads, source selection, or programming purpose.
Breaking out every module pin does not modify any assigned GPIO or the documented candidate GPIO pool.
The source decision does not affect I2C cable length, speed, pull-ups, series resistors, or resistor placement.
General ESP32-S3 platform reuse and full pin breakout do not change the switched 5V rail's enable GPIO, control behavior, converter, loads, or operating pattern.
The source does not alter DCDC1 voltage, current rating, normal-operation role, downstream target voltage, or diode-drop compensation.
The mention of buttons in possible future projects does not change the current panel reset connector, mounting, or electrical action.
